summary: Extracted the Start Run click-handler body (~55 lines) into a new closure-scoped helper `_handleStartRun(startBtn, planInput, resultsEl)` defined inside `renderOrchestrator()`.

The helper carries a full JSDoc block with a 'Closure dependencies (from renderOrchestrator() scope):' section listing allChecksPassed (mutated), refreshQueue (read-only), renderPreflightResults (read-only), and _orchStatusPollCleanups (mutated).
The original startBtn.addEventListener body is replaced with a single one-line delegation: `startBtn.addEventListener('click', function () { _handleStartRun(startBtn, planInput, resultsEl); });`
Updated the file-header module comment to document _handleStartRun() alongside the four existing renderQueueTable helpers.
All 28 existing orchestrator-view tests pass without modification.

comments.note: No observations — code in the touched files is clean and consistent. The extraction follows the exact same closure-scoped helper convention used for _clearSuccessBanner, _buildQueueHtml, _bindQueueActions, and _mountLogPreviews, keeping the codebase uniform.

summary: Verified all 5 Acceptance Criteria via direct code inspection of mcp-server/gui/public/views/orchestrator.js.
AC-1 PASS: _handleStartRun() is defined as a closure-scoped function at line 178, inside renderOrchestrator().
AC-2 PASS: The Start Run click listener at line 237 is a single one-line delegation: startBtn.addEventListener('click', function () { _handleStartRun(startBtn, planInput, resultsEl); });

AC-3 PASS: The JSDoc 'Closure dependencies (from renderOrchestrator() scope):' block at lines 159–173 lists all four closed-over variables — allChecksPassed (mutated), refreshQueue (read-only), renderPreflightResults (read-only), _orchStatusPollCleanups (mutated) — with correct annotations.

AC-4 PASS: Start Run functionality is fully preserved. The handler validates planPath and allChecksPassed, calls API.orchestratorStart(planPath, false), shows success banner + PID, clears input, calls refreshQueue(), and pushes a setInterval cleanup into _orchStatusPollCleanups. On failure, re-renders preflight results.
AC-5 PASS: All 28 orchestrator-view.test.ts tests pass without modification (vitest exit code 0, 178ms).

Edge case review: guard clause (!planPath || !allChecksPassed) prevents double-submit and empty-input submission. MAX_STATUS_POLLS=15 caps the polling window at 30s. The cleanup push to _orchStatusPollCleanups ensures polls are cancelled on full re-render.

comments.note: No observations — implementation is clean and consistent with the established closure-scoped helper pattern. The JSDoc block is thorough with correct mutated/read-only annotations on all four closed-over variables. The guard clause and double-submit protection are solid.

summary: Reviewed mcp-server/gui/public/views/orchestrator.js in full (462 lines). The _handleStartRun() extraction is clean, idiomatic, and consistent with the four existing renderQueueTable closure-scoped helpers.

One-line delegation at line 237 is clean. The trailing .then() 'finally' pattern at lines 231–233 is correct ES5 idiom and consistent with the preflight handler.

The decision to pass startBtn, planInput, resultsEl as explicit parameters (while allChecksPassed etc. are closed-over) is a deliberate architectural choice: DOM references that are also in scope as parameters make the helper self-contained and testable. comments.note: The .catch().then() 'finally' idiom at lines 231–233 of _handleStartRun() is correct and intentional, consistent with the preflight handler's identical pattern at lines 148–151. Future contributors unfamiliar with ES5 promise chains may read this as an always-running finally block — worth keeping as-is for consistency but could benefit from a brief inline comment if the project ever adds a contributor guide.

[documentation-forward] The _handleStartRun() JSDoc @param section documents startBtn, planInput, and resultsEl as parameters, but the Closure dependencies block (which lists allChecksPassed, refreshQueue, renderPreflightResults, _orchStatusPollCleanups) does not include a clarifying note explaining that resultsEl is absent from that list because it is passed as a parameter rather than captured from the outer scope. A one-line note on the resultsEl @param line — e.g. '(passed as parameter; not captured from closure)' — would prevent future readers from wondering why it is not listed in the closure-dependencies section.
